points.formation: N (받침 O) + 은 · N (받침 X) + 는

explanation.id: 은/는 menandai topik kalimat, yaitu hal yang sedang dibicarakan. Pakai 은 setelah kata yang berakhiran konsonan (받침 O), 는 setelah kata yang berakhiran vokal (받침 X).
explanation.en: 은/는 marks the topic, what the sentence is about. Use 은 after a word ending in a consonant (받침 O) and 는 after a vowel (받침 X).

points.formation: N (받침 O) + 이에요 · N (받침 X) + 예요

explanation.id: Bentuk sopan sehari-hari dari 이다 "adalah". Pakai 이에요 setelah konsonan dan 예요 setelah vokal. Sebagai pertanyaan, cukup naikkan nada di akhir.
explanation.en: The everyday polite form of 이다 "to be". Use 이에요 after a consonant and 예요 after a vowel. As a question, just raise your voice at the end.

tr.en: My father is an office worker.

points.formation: N (받침 O) + 이 아니에요 · N (받침 X) + 가 아니에요

explanation.id: Bentuk negatif dari 이에요/예요. Kata bendanya diberi 이 (setelah konsonan) atau 가 (setelah vokal), lalu 아니에요.
explanation.en: The negative of 이에요/예요. The noun takes 이 (after a consonant) or 가 (after a vowel), then 아니에요.

tr.en: That person is not a doctor.

points.formation: N (받침 O) + 이 · N (받침 X) + 가

explanation.id: 이/가 menandai subjek, yaitu siapa atau apa yang melakukan atau mengalami sesuatu. Sering dipakai dengan kata sifat dan dengan 있어요/없어요, dan untuk informasi baru.
explanation.en: 이/가 marks the subject, who or what does or is something. It is common with adjectives and with 있어요/없어요, and for new information.

tr.en: My younger sibling goes to school.

meaning.id: ada, punya / tidak ada, tidak punya
meaning.en: there is, have / there isn't, don't have

points.formation: N이/가 + 있어요 · N이/가 + 없어요

explanation.id: 있어요 berarti "ada" atau "punya", 없어요 kebalikannya. Hal yang ada atau dimiliki diberi 이/가.
explanation.en: 있어요 means "there is" or "to have"; 없어요 is the opposite. What exists or is had takes 이/가.

tr.id: Hari ini saya tidak punya waktu.

tr.en: There are students in the classroom.

tr.id: Saya tidak punya uang, jadi tidak bisa membeli.
tr.en: I have no money, so I can't buy it.

points.formation: N (받침 O) + 을 · N (받침 X) + 를

explanation.id: 을/를 menandai objek, yaitu hal yang dikenai pekerjaan: yang dimakan, dibaca, dilihat. Kata kerjanya selalu di akhir kalimat.
explanation.en: 을/를 marks the object, what the action is done to: what is eaten, read, seen. The verb always comes last.

points.formation: ㅏ, ㅗ + 아요 · ㅓ, ㅜ, ㅡ, ㅣ … + 어요 · 하다 → 해요

explanation.id: Akhiran sopan yang paling sering dipakai. Buang 다, lalu lihat vokal terakhir: ㅏ atau ㅗ mendapat 아요, vokal lain 어요, dan 하다 menjadi 해요. Vokal yang bertemu sering melebur: 가 + 아요 → 가요, 보 + 아요 → 봐요, 마시 + 어요 → 마셔요.
explanation.en: The most common polite ending. Drop 다 and look at the last vowel: ㅏ or ㅗ takes 아요, any other vowel 어요, and 하다 becomes 해요. Meeting vowels often merge: 가 + 아요 → 가요, 보 + 아요 → 봐요, 마시 + 어요 → 마셔요.

points.formation: 학교에 가요 · 집에 있어요 · 세 시에

explanation.id: 에 menunjukkan tujuan (ke), tempat sesuatu berada (di, dengan 있어요/없어요) dan waktu (pada). Untuk tempat melakukan kegiatan, pakai 에서.
explanation.en: 에 marks a destination (to), where something is (with 있어요/없어요) and a time (at, on). For where an action happens, use 에서.

tr.en: I am going to Busan tomorrow.
I am going to Seoul tomorrow.
The cat is in the room.

meaning.en: at, in (where something is done), from

points.formation: N + 에서 + V · 도서관에서 공부해요

explanation.id: 에서 menandai tempat sebuah kegiatan dilakukan: belajar di perpustakaan, makan di restoran. 에서 juga berarti "dari" untuk asal.
explanation.en: 에서 marks where an action happens: studying at the library, eating at a restaurant. It also means "from" a place.

points.formation: 저는 → 저도 · 커피를 → 커피도

explanation.id: 도 berarti "juga". 도 menggantikan penanda 은/는, 이/가 atau 을/를, jadi bukan 저는도 tetapi 저도.
explanation.en: 도 means "also". It replaces 은/는, 이/가 or 을/를, so it is 저도, not 저는도.

tr.id: Saya membeli apel dan juga pisang.
tr.en: I bought apples and bananas too.
My younger sibling is tall too.

points.formation: N + 하고 · N (받침 X) + 와 · N (받침 O) + 과

explanation.id: 하고 dan 와/과 menghubungkan dua kata benda ("dan") atau berarti "bersama". 하고 lebih santai dalam percakapan; 와 dipakai setelah vokal, 과 setelah konsonan.
explanation.en: 하고 and 와/과 join two nouns ("and") or mean "with". 하고 is more casual and common in speech; 와 follows a vowel, 과 a consonant.

tr.en: There is a book and a notebook.

tr.id: Saya pergi ke pasar bersama ibu.
tr.en: I went to the market with my mother.

points.formation: ㅏ, ㅗ + 았어요 · ㅓ, ㅜ, ㅡ, ㅣ … + 었어요 · 하다 → 했어요

explanation.id: Untuk sesuatu yang sudah terjadi. Sama seperti -아요/어요: ㅏ atau ㅗ mendapat 았어요, vokal lain 었어요, 하다 menjadi 했어요. Vokal juga melebur: 가 → 갔어요, 보 → 봤어요.
explanation.en: For something that already happened. As with -아요/어요: ㅏ or ㅗ takes 았어요, other vowels 었어요, and 하다 becomes 했어요. Vowels merge too: 가 → 갔어요, 보 → 봤어요.

tr.en: I met a friend at the weekend.

tr.id: Tahun lalu saya pergi ke Korea.
tr.en: I went to Korea last year.

points.formation: 안 + V/A-아요/어요 · V/A + 지 않아요 · N하다 → N 안 해요

explanation.id: Ada dua cara mengatakan "tidak": 안 di depan kata kerja atau kata sifat (lebih umum dalam percakapan), atau -지 않아요 di belakangnya. Pada kata kerja benda + 하다, 안 masuk sebelum 하다: 공부 안 해요.
explanation.en: Two ways to say "not": 안 before the verb or adjective (more common in speech), or -지 않아요 after it. In noun + 하다 verbs, 안 goes before 하다: 공부 안 해요.

points.formation: 가다 → 가고 싶어요 · 먹다 → 먹고 싶어요

explanation.id: Untuk mengatakan keinginan sendiri atau menanyakan keinginan lawan bicara. Buang 다 dan tambahkan 고 싶어요; tidak ada perubahan bunyi.
explanation.en: Says what you want to do, or asks what the listener wants to do. Drop 다 and add 고 싶어요; nothing else changes.

tr.en: I want to go to Korea.
What do you want to eat?
I want to rest at the weekend.

points.formation: 받침 X + ㄹ 거예요 · 받침 O + 을 거예요 · 살다 → 살 거예요

explanation.id: Untuk rencana atau perkiraan masa depan. Setelah vokal, ㄹ menempel pada suku kata terakhir (가 → 갈 거예요); setelah konsonan tambahkan 을 (먹 → 먹을 거예요); kata yang sudah berakhiran ㄹ tetap (살 → 살 거예요).
explanation.en: For plans or guesses about the future. After a vowel, ㄹ joins the last syllable (가 → 갈 거예요); after a consonant add 을 (먹 → 먹을 거예요); a stem already ending in ㄹ stays (살 → 살 거예요).

tr.en: I will meet a friend tomorrow.

tr.id: Akhir pekan saya akan beristirahat di rumah.
tr.en: I will rest at home at the weekend.
I will read a book tomorrow.

tr.id: Bulan depan saya akan pergi ke Korea.
tr.en: I will go to Korea next month.

points.formation: 받침 X + 세요 · 받침 O + 으세요 · 열다 → 여세요

explanation.id: Permintaan atau perintah yang sopan. Setelah vokal tambahkan 세요, setelah konsonan 으세요; ㄹ di akhir batang kata hilang (만들다 → 만드세요). Beberapa kata punya bentuk khusus: 먹다 → 드세요, 자다 → 주무세요.
explanation.en: A polite request or instruction. Add 세요 after a vowel and 으세요 after a consonant; a final ㄹ drops (만들다 → 만드세요). Some verbs have their own form: 먹다 → 드세요, 자다 → 주무세요.

points.formation: V-아/어 + 주세요 · 하다 → 해 주세요

explanation.id: Meminta orang lain melakukan sesuatu untuk kita. Bentuk -아/어 sama dengan -아요/어요 tanpa 요: 열다 → 열어 주세요, 하다 → 해 주세요.
explanation.en: Asks someone to do something for you. The -아/어 form is -아요/어요 without 요: 열다 → 열어 주세요, 하다 → 해 주세요.

points.formation: 먹다 → 먹고 · 싸다 → 싸고

explanation.id: Menggabungkan dua kalimat: dua sifat atau kegiatan ("dan"), atau kegiatan yang berurutan ("lalu"). Bentuk waktu ditaruh di kata kerja terakhir.
explanation.en: Joins two clauses: two qualities or actions ("and"), or actions in order ("and then"). The tense goes on the last verb.

tr.en: This restaurant is cheap and good.

tr.id: Saya makan lalu pergi ke sekolah.
tr.en: I eat and then go to school.
My room is big and clean.
I did my homework and then slept.

points.formation: 어렵다 → 어렵지만 · 오다 → 오지만

explanation.id: Menghubungkan dua hal yang berlawanan, seperti "tetapi" atau "meskipun". Buang 다 dan tambahkan 지만.
explanation.en: Joins two contrasting clauses, like "but" or "although". Drop 다 and add 지만.

tr.id: Meskipun hujan, saya pergi ke sekolah.
tr.en: It's raining, but I go to school.
These clothes are expensive but pretty.

tr.id: Saya lapar tetapi tidak punya waktu.
tr.en: I'm hungry but have no time.

points.formation: V/A-아/어 + 서 · 하다 → 해서

explanation.id: Memberi alasan ("karena ..., jadi") atau menghubungkan dua kegiatan yang berkaitan (bertemu lalu menonton bersama). Bentuk -아/어 sama dengan -아요/어요 tanpa 요; bentuk lampau tidak dipakai sebelum -아서/어서.
explanation.en: Gives a reason ("because ..., so") or links two connected actions (meet and then watch together). The -아/어 form is -아요/어요 without 요; no past tense goes before -아서/어서.

tr.en: I was hungry, so I ate.

tr.id: Saya bertemu teman lalu menonton film bersama.
tr.en: I met a friend and we watched a movie.

tr.id: Hari ini saya sibuk, jadi tidak bisa pergi.
tr.en: I'm busy today, so I can't go.

points.formation: 받침 X + ㄹ 수 있어요 · 받침 O + 을 수 있어요

explanation.id: Mengatakan kemampuan atau kemungkinan. Bentuk -(으)ㄹ dibuat sama seperti pada -(으)ㄹ 거예요, lalu 수 있어요 (bisa) atau 수 없어요 (tidak bisa).
explanation.en: Says what someone can or cannot do. The -(으)ㄹ form is made as in -(으)ㄹ 거예요, then 수 있어요 (can) or 수 없어요 (cannot).

tr.id: Hari ini kita tidak bisa bertemu.

points.formation: 받침 X + ㅂ니다 · 받침 O + 습니다 · N + 입니다

explanation.id: Bentuk paling resmi, dipakai dalam berita, pidato, rapat dan salam tertentu. Setelah vokal, ㅂ menempel pada suku kata terakhir (가 → 갑니다); setelah konsonan tambahkan 습니다 (먹 → 먹습니다). Kata benda + 입니다 berarti "adalah".
explanation.en: The most formal style, used in news, speeches, meetings and set greetings. After a vowel, ㅂ joins the last syllable (가 → 갑니다); after a consonant add 습니다 (먹 → 먹습니다). Noun + 입니다 means "is".

tr.en: I am reading a book now.
